label: Weapon traits
description: Combinable twists on a weapon. A card's weapon has up to three; a researched weapon up to four.

terms.label: Splash
terms.description: Damages an area around the impact.
terms.source_rule: Set it when the sources say the hit hurts everything in an area around the impact. Leave it off when they say it hits one target at a time, call the area tiny or very small, or disagree. An area effect that does no damage, such as an area stun, is not splash. A radius figure in the sources counts as saying the hit hurts an area. Tiny or very small must be the sources' own words, never a judgement from the figure.

terms.label: Pierce
terms.description: Passes through the first target to hit others behind it.

terms.label: Chain
terms.description: Jumps from the first target to nearby ones.

terms.label: Damage over time
terms.description: Keeps hurting the target after the hit: burning, corrosion, damage from inside.

terms.label: Lingering zone
terms.description: Leaves a hazard on the ground (fire, gas, nanites) that hurts whoever stands in it.

terms.label: Charge-up
terms.description: Hold to charge, then release: a stronger shot, or a burst of more shots.
terms.source_rule: Set it when the sources say the player holds the trigger to build the shot up before it fires. Energy that builds while the weapon keeps firing, released by another key or by itself, is not charge-up: describe it in the summary.

terms.label: Spin-up
terms.description: Fires slowly at first and speeds up while held.
terms.source_rule: Set it when the sources say or show the rate of fire rising while the weapon keeps firing; continuous-fire stages in a stats table count, because the rise is how it fires.

terms.label: Overheat
terms.description: Fires continuously until it overheats, then must cool down.

terms.label: Magazine
terms.description: Fires a set number of shots, then must reload, or wait for its ammo to come back on its own.
terms.source_rule: Set it only when the sources show the reload as part of how this weapon fights: they describe it firing a burst or salvo and then stopping to reload, name its reload or clip as a strength or weakness of this weapon, or say its ammo runs out and comes back on its own. A reload time in a stats table, a passing mention, or a comparison of how often two guns reload does not count. A weapon that holds one shot per reload (a single-shot launcher or cannon) never gets it for that reload: its reload is its rate of fire, so say in the summary, in words, how long it takes.

terms.label: Homing
terms.description: Shots steer toward the target.
terms.source_rule: Only for shots that steer themselves after firing with no lock step and no steering by the shooter, such as smart rockets. Never with lock-on or guided delivery, which already steer.

terms.label: Knockback
terms.description: Pushes targets away.

terms.label: Slow
terms.description: Slows the target.

terms.label: Root / pin
terms.description: The target can't move but can still fire and use abilities.

terms.label: Silence / disarm
terms.description: The target can move but can't fire or use abilities.

terms.label: Stun
terms.description: The target can't do anything for a very short time. T2 and up, on a medium or longer cooldown.

terms.label: Suppress
terms.description: Sustained fire pins targets: slows them and spoils their aim while under fire.
terms.source_rule: Set it only when the sources say this weapon's own fire, with no ability in use, pins or suppresses targets as one of its main jobs, as with a machine gun built for it. A weapon that pins only now and then, or only while an ability is active, does not get it; that ability links the suppress-with-fire pattern instead.

terms.label: Mark
terms.description: Tags the target so the whole team sees it and hits it harder for a time.

terms.label: Minimum range
terms.description: Can't hit targets inside a dead zone close to the unit.

terms.label: Friendly fire
terms.description: Its splash or penetration also hurts allies.

terms.label: Limited ammo
terms.description: Carries a fixed stock that does not come back by itself; only a teammate, a station or a pickup refills it, if anything does. A stock that refills on its own over time is magazine.
terms.source_rule: When the unit has the limited-ammo resource, give this trait only to the weapons that draw on it while others do not (a 'Mech's autocannon and missiles beside its lasers); when every weapon draws on it, the resource alone says so.

terms.label: Shield-breaker
terms.description: Deals bonus damage to shields and barriers.

terms.label: Heals on hit
terms.description: Damage dealt restores the attacker's health.
terms.notes: Healing by hurting, on the weapon itself. Not the heal-self pattern (a heal on a key) or the self-repair armour model (health that comes back on its own).

terms.label: Anti-air
terms.description: Built to bring down aircraft: a weapon whose family reaches low air can, with this trait, reach high air too. Lobbed, dropped, placed and melee shots never hit high fliers, so it never goes with those deliveries.
examples: Red Alert 3: the Multigunner IFV's default missiles and its Archer Maiden bow reach every aircraft
PlanetSide 2: anti-aircraft machine guns, which the game gives a damage class of their own
terms.source_rule: On a researched weapon, set it exactly when its can_target includes high-air, whatever the family. On flak, guided missiles and autocannons it marks what the weapon is for; on other families it is also what lets the weapon reach high air.
